audit.whatIsWrong: Every chart row disagreed with the packet chart and with the whys paragraph printed under it, and the EVEN label sat next to a 6/10 difficulty rating on a 52.26% win rate.
audit.why: The whys text is already correct and specific: whys[0] says concede the level-1 contest (Maokai), whys[1] calls it 'a coin-flip' (Skill), whys[2] says 'the lane stays even' (Skill), whys[3]/[4]/[5] describe you winning the extended trade, the all-in and the Riftmaker window (Gragas), whys[6] says 'the duel evens out' (Skill). That is exactly the packet chart. The stored sides read Skill/Gragas/Gragas/Skill/Skill/Gragas/Gragas — wrong on six of seven rows. Separately, 52.26% over 1018 games is a genuinely even lane, so EVEN is right but 6/10 is not.
audit.corrected: Chart flipped to Maokai / Skill / Skill / Gragas / Gragas / Gragas / Skill with ratings 3-5-5-7-7-7-5; diffRating 6/10 to 5/10; carryRating 7/10 to 6/10, which matches the page's own 'low-threat tank kit' description of him.

audit.whatIsWrong: The phase rows were boilerplate ('Q-poke from range wins level 1 outright') and carried no timings, which is why they had drifted away from the content layer.
audit.why: Sapling Toss throws 1100 and is his level-1 zoning tool; Bramble Smash is a 7/6.5/6/5.5/5s knockback; Twisted Advance is 14/13/12/11/10s; his R is 130/110/90 at 3000 range. Your all-in runs off a 12-14s Body Slam and a 100/85/70 Cask, so the trade windows are set by his W timer, not by a generic 'lane-control window'.
audit.corrected: All six rewritten phase whys now carry the real numbers and match the content-layer stage owners.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two decisive interactions were absent everywhere on the page: Twisted Advance makes him untargetable for the duration of the dash, and Sap Magic's cooldown is reduced every time he is struck by an enemy spell — not only when he casts.
audit.why: Untargetability means a Cask or Body Slam timed onto his engage simply misses him mid-dash; the correct timing is before the cast or after he lands, and the page told you to 'dodge it' without ever saying why chasing the dash fails. The Sap Magic clause is worse for a poke champion: every Barrel Roll you land on him accelerates his sustain, which is precisely the pattern the rest of the page recommends. That reframes the poke war and supports the Executioner's Calling line the itemization already calls for.
audit.corrected: Untargetability and the spell-struck Sap Magic reduction written into breakdown.cooldowns; the Sap Magic point also written into wants.foe[1].

audit.why: The two suspectNames flagged by the packet are false positives: Maokai's W really is Twisted Advance and Gragas' R really is Explosive Cask. Both were left alone.

edits.before: Q-poke from range wins level 1 outright. Identify how Maokai contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Level 1 is his — Sapling Toss reaches 1100 and zones the wave before Drunken Rage exists. Concede the push and farm.

edits.before: W damage reduction + sustain flips his return trade. Only take the trade when Maokai's Twisted Advance is down.
edits.after: W gives you a real trade, but Sap Magic sustain and a 7s Bramble Smash knockback answer it — whoever casts first wins.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Maokai must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: He can Twisted Advance you onto the sapling field on 14s while your Q is still 8s — the lane stays even until W is maxed.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Twisted Advance's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are yours: W maxed and Happy Hour out-sustain the sapling chip — commit the extended trade the moment Twisted Advance is down.

edits.before: Explosive Cask both finishes kills and deletes engages — you choose the fight. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Maokai's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Level 6 is your all-in: Body Slam stun, W-empowered auto, Q detonate, and Cask to finish — he cannot escape it without Twisted Advance up.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Maokai carry threat 7/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Two items on he is a tankier double-CC frontline and the duel evens out — your Cask becomes a peel tool, not a kill button.

edits.before: - Maokai Twisted Advance: matchup-defining — His lock-on root. Dodge it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Maokai Twisted Advance: matchup-defining — 14s at rank 1, and he is untargetable through the dash. Dodge it. - Sap Magic: every spell you land on him shortens its cooldown. - Cask: kill windows only.

edits.before: Overall difficulty: 6/10. The lane is decided by how well you track Twisted Advance and how disciplined your pattern is.
edits.after: Overall difficulty: 5/10. The lane turns on dodging a 14s Twisted Advance and out-sustaining Sap Magic with Happy Hour.

edits.before: Carry threat: 7/10. If Maokai gets ahead, shift from winning trades to wave control, vision, and jungle play.
edits.after: Carry threat: 6/10. If Maokai gets ahead, shift from winning trades to wave control, vision, and jungle play.

notes: The content layer for this matchup was already good (real ability names throughout); the full layer was untouched boilerplate and its level chart contradicted the content prose on six of seven rows. Chart flip proposed as one atomic group. I did NOT write any claim that Nature's Grasp blocks movement or dashes: the kit derives a 'terrain' flag but Riot's description only says the wall advances, damages and roots. Same restraint on the grounding flag derived for Bramble Smash.
